papers.title: CONCEPTUAL EMERGENCE & GENERATIVE INTELLIGENCE AT THE LIMIT Living Concept Civilization — Flagship Research Monograph 06 STARLI / White Rainbow Civilization · October 2026 ABSTRACT When do interactions among concepts, models, tools and people produce a genuinely new, independently verifiable capacity rather than a novel label or a misleading evaluation threshold? This English-language research monograph develops a falsifiable program for conceptual emergence and generative intelligence. Its research three-coupling is Interaction Generation × New-Function Identification × Counterfactual Verification. The proposed emergence expression compares held-out capability improvement with the strongest viable baseline and a contamination penalty, with all terms requiring operational definition and appropriate normalization before use. RESEARCH DESIGN The volume studies both smooth scaling and possible discontinuities, evaluation-metric sensitivity, training-data leakage, compositional generalization, simple-rule baselines, factorial component ablation, multi-agent collaboration, correlated errors, human-AI complementarity, multimodal grounding, causal interventions, tool-dependence, calibration, cross-model reproducibility, governance, and intergenerational handoff. A claimed capability must survive preregistered unseen tasks, strong comparators, counterfactual perturbations and independent reproduction. A fluent explanation, a generated new term or a model's assertion of consciousness is not evidence of functional emergence. MONOGRAPH STRUCTURE The 82 research chapters each present one distinct proposed chapter-wide operational equation, followed by twelve independently paginated study sections. Thirty advanced physics derivation routes appear in the preface with three-dimensional conceptual diagrams; they are existing physics statements within specified domains and do not establish laws of language or awareness. The concluding 200 Research Gates and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos each feature one of 233 distinct physical equation anchors. These equations are methodological contrasts and educational prompts, not proof of the emergence hypotheses. A separate Excel workbook indexes chapters, sections, gates, candidate mechanisms and physics anchors. EVIDENCE AND ETHICS This monograph is a theoretical and experimental research agenda. It reports no new trials, controlled effects or validated discoveries; all proposed mechanisms, metrics, forecasts and outcomes are UNVERIFIED until independently tested. The distinction between appearance under a chosen test and a robust new function must be maintained. Consent, intellectual provenance, lawful data use, security and affected persons' right to refuse are hard constraints rather than offsettable penalties. OPEN RESEARCH INVITATION Research Gates reserve space for questions that can be rejected, refined or answered by future researchers. Phoenix Answer Embryos are provisional designs that can be falsified, decomposed, recombined or responsibly retired. The goal is not a permanent claim that machines awaken or that thought obeys physical equations; it is an enduring, contestable toolkit for recognizing and scrutinizing useful new functions. FOUNDATIONS Project source: Living Concept Civilization — Eighteen Tri-Coupled Flagship Research Programs, v2.0 (2026-10-13), Flagship 06. (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.15004. Chollet, On the Measure of Intelligence (2019), https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.01547. Wilkinson et al., FAIR Guiding Principles (2016), https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18.

papers.title: STIGMERGIC SWARM MANUFACTURING UNDER QUANTUM MEASUREMENT UNCERTAINTY AT THE LIMIT A Research Architecture for Local Trace Coordination, Uncertainty-Aware Manufacturing, Reference Integrity, and Recoverable Collective Control

In manufacturing, these marks may designate reserved workspaces, completed operations, defects, material scarcity, assembly dependencies, inspection requirements, or unresolved quality questions. papers.title: The Disciplinary Language Transfer Problem: How Psychological Vocabulary Produces Governance Failures in AI Agent Deployment
papers.summary: The vocabulary used to describe AI agents in governance contexts — learning, memory, values, compliance, identity, trust — is borrowed from psychological and organizational science, contributing to systematic failures in how organizations deploy, oversee, and hold agents accountable. This paper argues that the problem is not merely terminological but epistemological: psychological vocabulary carries an "invisible grammar" of its home discipline into governance discourse, calibrating frameworks to a metaphysical entity that does not exist in current AI architectures. We call this the disciplinary language transfer problem. Drawing on Wittgenstein's concept of language games, Kuhn's paradigm-laden observation, Haraway's situated knowledge, and Star and Griesemer's boundary object theory, we show that the transfer operates at three levels — epistemological assumptions, theoretical constructs, and surface vocabulary — each requiring a different remediation. We characterize six foundational epistemological assumptions embedded in Western psychological governance discourse, trace their origin in specific philosophical traditions, and show why each fails when applied to systems without developmental continuity. The paper's practical output is an actionable Disciplinary Audit — a six-question governance document scan operationalized through a comprehensive translation taxonomy of thirt

papers.title: BGVD-State: Replayable middleware for evidence-gated handoffs in third-party software security review
papers.summary: Third-party software security review is iterative: models, tools, and people raise suspected-risk candidates, test them against evidence, and hand the evolving review state to subsequent reviewers. Conversation logs preserve observations but may lose track of which candidates remain active, which evidence is current, which paths failed, and which decision controls reporting. BGVD-State is open-source, model-independent middleware for making these handoffs replayable and auditable. It preserves submitted event sequences, reconstructs candidate and evidence lifecycles, retains failed paths, persists checkpoints, applies an evidence-based reporting gate, and generates a handoff package. In a local review of fixed TypeScript, Django, and ECC revisions, 22 records reconstructed six suspected-risk candidates; a subsequent event completed the final candidate’s evidence-supported disposition. Automated regression tests and offline replay check the implementation, including rejection of invalid events without residual state changes. Separate continuation experiments compare model-maintained memory representations: schema-guided memory outperformed matched free-form memory on selected high-state-pressure fixtures, whereas information-equivalent prose tied and a cross-family source-audit setting did not reproduce the advantage. papers.title: The Property Management Industry Has a Memory Problem
papers.summary: UK residential block management has a memory problem. Knowledge about a building, such as why systems were specified, why works were deferred, what was tried before and what it cost, accumulates in the heads of property managers, in inboxes and in disconnected systems, and is routinely lost when people or managing agents change. Drawing on knowledge-management theory, research on construction-to-operations handover and on multi-owned housing, and five building handovers observed by the author, this paper argues that failures of organisational memory contribute to persistent problems in leasehold management. It proposes a Building Knowledge Hierarchy (data, information, knowledge, organisational memory and building intelligence) and a Persistent Building Knowledge Model, in which knowledge attaches to the building and its assets rather than to the individual, document or system through which it arrives, and in which provenance, confidence and the reasoning behind decisions are preserved. It positions the model alongside the statutory Golden Thread for higher-risk buildings, arguing that its principles should extend to a building’s wider operational and financial history. It builds on asset-information approaches such as ISO 19650, digital twins and building logbooks, while addressing the difficulty of maintaining usable knowledge across fragmented ownership, incomplete records a

papers.title: Breaking Bottlenecks in Solid Electrolyte Discovery With Large Artificial Intelligence Models
papers.summary: Solid electrolytes (SEs) are central to next-generation metal batteries, yet their discovery remains constrained by fragmented data, limited transferability of simulations, and slow experimental iteration. Unlike catalysis, where surface reactivity dominates, SEs require simultaneous optimization of bulk ion transport, defect chemistry, mechanical integrity, and interfacial stability. Here, we outline a framework for autonomous SE discovery enabled by large artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and large language models (LLMs). We discuss the evolution from static materials databases to dynamic, self-updating knowledge systems, the role of MLIPs in bridging density functional theory (DFT) and long-timescale ion migration, and the emergence of LLMs as engines for literature mining, hypothesis generation, and scientific reasoning. We further describe a closed-loop architecture integrating AI-driven candidate design, multiscale simulation, uncertainty-aware selection, and experimental validation. Such systems shift SE research from intuition-guided exploration to data-informed, self-improving cycles. We conclude by highlighting challenges in data standardization, interfacial complexity, and reproducibility, and we propose design principles for building autonomous laboratories for solid-state battery materials.

papers.title: Always On: Dots and the Safeguards Behind AI That Works While You Sleep
papers.summary: Always On: Dots and the Safeguards Behind AI That Works While You Sleep examines OpenAI's newly announced dots: persistent AI agents designed to continue working toward a user's goals after the chat window closes. The report investigates how these agents operate, what safeguards govern their actions, and where important uncertainties remain. It examines their cloud-based workspaces, connected applications, proactive research capabilities, action permissions, safety reviews, persistent memory, and exposure to prompt injection. A central focus is the tension between autonomy and oversight. An agent that can work independently offers convenience, but it can also read sensitive information, retain context that users cannot individually inspect, and take consequential actions through connected systems. The report also examines research published shortly before the launch describing self-replicating prompt injections in simulated agent environments. It distinguishes those reported experimental findings from demonstrated real-world incidents and does not claim that this behavior has been observed in deployed dots. Drawing on public documentation and independent reporting, the investigation explores four recurring tensions: autonomy versus oversight, memory versus transparency, reach versus risk, and candor versus responsibility. It also considers the implications of agents communicati

papers.title: Quality Evaluation of Clustering-Based Process Model Discovery Using Event Log Similarity
papers.summary: Model discovery discovers process models from event logs, but directly discovered models are usually complex and hard to interpret. Trace clustering tackles this problem by splitting an event log into smaller sublogs, each of which can support the discovery of simpler models. In this setting, clustering quality means that the obtained sublogs are behaviorally coherent and sufficiently different to achieve meaningful process model discovery. Existing evaluation depends on F-Measure, but it is dependent on the chosen discovery algorithm, requires costly fitness and precision computation, etc. To overcome these disadvantages, in this paper, we propose a clustering evaluation approach as a surrogate complement to model-quality evaluation rather than an alternative to existing model-quality measures such as fitness, precision, and F-Measure. Specifically, this clustering evaluation approach assesses clustering quality on the inter-sublog event log similarity, rather than the discovered process models. These are instantiated with three state-of-the-art log-similarity metrics. Our experiments using four real-life event logs show that the obtained scores are strongly negatively correlated with the F-Measure in most of the cases and have reduced the evaluation time by a factor of 47,547 down to 63 ms. These results indicate that the proposed framework provides an efficient and discovery

papers.title: Agent Foundry: A Boundary-Preserving Architecture for Governed Agentic Platforms
papers.summary: Agent frameworks expose tools, delegation, memory and human approval, yet the controls attached to a request (identity, tenant, scopes, budgets, deadlines, rate limits, fail behavior) are routinely lost at execution boundaries: delegation, threads, streaming, resume, caching, retrieval and adapter exports. We present Agent Foundry, an open-source Python platform whose architecture is organized around one principle: every control is a property of the request’s execution scope, not an argument that each layer must remember to pass. We formalize this as the Governed Execution Contract (GEC), a meet-semilattice of control scopes with seven invariants, and prove that delegation can only attenuate authority, that deny rules can only tighten resolution, that per-principal rate limits are exact under arbi-trary thread interleavings, that every call yields exactly one audited decision even when the policy source is unreachable, and that admission partitions by principal without cross-shard coordination. On AgentGovBench, a public 48-scenario gov-ernance benchmark, Agent Foundry passes 48/48 in 10 of 10 repetitions, against 46/48 for the best published governed configuration and 13/48 for each of 7 pub-lished framework-native runners; run through the same harness, Microsoft’s Agent Governance Toolkit scores at most 46/48 and Bounded Agents 36/48, and on a 24-scenario suite authored blind

papers.title: Reflective AI: A Conceptual Framework for Second-Order Reflection and Temporal Self-Understanding
papers.summary: This paper proposes Reflective AI: an architecture in which an intelligent agent can examine not only its recorded prior reasoning contexts, but also the history of its subsequent interpretations of those contexts. The conceptual starting point is the difficulty of establishing subjective self-awareness in another system. The continuing sense of human identity across interruptions in conscious experience suggests a narrower, functionally investigable question: how can a system connect what it once knew, believed and anticipated with what later occurred? The architecture retains selective, immutable records of the information, assumptions, goals, forecasts and documented reasoning links relevant to decisions; it does not attempt to capture every machine computation. Multiple later interpretations are stored separately, and second-order reflection evaluates whether current interpretations and the criteria for selecting evidence should change. Reflection is event-triggered and directed towards identifying missing knowledge and improving future decisions, not endless introspection. This paper situates the proposal within existing work on autobiographical memory, prospective simulation, metacognition and reflective agents, and outlines a feasible comparative evaluation without claiming that the system would possess subjective consciousness.

papers.title: Educational Recommender Systems for Metacognitive and Self-Regulated Learning Support: An Algorithmic Systematic Review
papers.summary: Recommender systems (RSs) increasingly support self-regulated learning (SRL) through personalized resources, feedback, and strategy recommendations. However, traditional content based and collaborative filtering approaches suffer from cold start problems, while machine or deep learning methods raise interpretability concerns and LLM-based recommenders require evaluation of explanation faithfulness and hallucinations. This systematic review examines SRL-oriented recommender algorithms from an algorithmic and pedagogical perspective. Six databases were searched using predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, yielding 25 eligible studies published between 2020 and 2025. The review traces the evolution from traditional filtering methods to machine or deep learning and emerging LLM-based approaches. Three major challenges were identified: cold start, limited explainability, and LLM hallucinations, alongside gaps in learner system interaction and metacognitive scaffolding. Future SRL-RS research should compare algorithms under controlled data sparsity, evaluate explanation faithfulness and source curation, preserve learner agency, integrate SRL strategies across three phases, and longitudinally assess SRL skill maintenance and transfer.

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: A cascaded probabilistic framework for stealth-aware MITRE ATT&CK path prediction in active directory adversary emulation
papers.summary: Abstract Proactive adversary emulation requires anticipating multi-step attack trajectories, yet existing approaches rely on static attack graphs or single-signal models that cannot jointly satisfy coherence, tactical realism, and evasiveness. We propose a cascaded probabilistic framework for MITRE ATT&CK technique-path prediction in Active Directory environments, where exhaustive enumeration is intractable. Its contribution is a three-stage architecture that decouples these objectives instead of blending them. Stage 1, a two-layer unidirectional LSTM trained on observed threat-actor chains, emits a five-candidate pool rather than one technique. Stage 2, an empirical Markov tactic-transition gate, admits only attested transitions, including self-loops and backward moves a strict linear kill chain excludes. Stage 3 re-ranks survivors against a detection-rule corpus, favoring evasive over merely probable techniques. Candidates are masked at inference to Windows-applicable techniques, so outputs are technique chains, not instantiated paths. Under a prefix-disjoint protocol in which no evaluation context occurs in training, the true continuation is retained in the five-candidate pool more often than by a first-order predictor or an exact prefix-lookup table on identical pairs. papers.title: Beyond access and algorithms: a curricular model for inquiry-driven student-AI engagement
papers.summary: Purpose This paper proposes a pedagogical framework for cultivating inquiry-driven agency in student engagement with artificial intelligence (AI). It addresses a gap in the AI-in-education literature, in which substantial scholarly attention to material access and algorithmic fairness has been accompanied by comparatively less sustained attention to the learner-side capacities that determine whether AI is engaged with critically or passively. The paper offers three connected contributions: a cyclical model of inquiry-driven learning, a four-phase curricular sequence for student-AI engagement, and an operational assessment counterpart that remains diagnostically meaningful in AI-mediated environments. Design/methodology/approach The paper employs an integrative conceptual approach in the tradition of model-paper scholarship (Jaakkola, 2020). It synthesises five bodies of literature: AI in education and AI literacy frameworks, critical scholarship on educational technology, foundational work on curiosity, dual-process cognition, and adaptive expertise, constructive-developmental theory, and research on question-asking in learning and authentic assessment. Sources were identified through targeted citation tracing supplemented by database searches. Theoretical resources are justified at the point of use rather than methodologically up front. papers.title: Potential role of irisin-mediated oxidative stress defense in systemic diseases
papers.summary: Oxidative stress arises when excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) overwhelm endogenous antioxidant defenses, leading to deleterious modifications of lipids, proteins, and DNA. Persistent oxidative stress is implicated in the pathogenesis of numerous chronic disorders, including cardiovascular diseases, neurodegenerative conditions, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and ischaemia–reperfusion (I/R) injury across multiple organs. Irisin, a myokine/adipokine proteolytically cleaved from fibronectin type III domain-containing protein 5 (FNDC5), was first characterized in 2012. Preclinical studies have increasingly demonstrated that irisin possesses potent antioxidant properties and exerts cytoprotective effects in diverse tissues. These antioxidant actions are mediated through multiple molecular mechanisms: activation of the nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) pathway with subsequent upregulation of cytoprotective enzymes such as haem oxygenase-1 (HO-1); sirtuin 3 (SIRT3)-dependent deacetylation and activation of mitochondrial superoxide dismutase 2 (SOD2); inhibition of pro-oxidant enzymes including NADPH oxidase (NOX); and modulation of mitochondrial fusion-fission dynamics to preserve mitochondrial homeostasis. Functionally, irisin initiates intracellular signalling cascades, including AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), PI3K/Akt, and MAPK pathways, primarily through b

papers.title: From plausible menus to trustworthy nutrition: a risk-proportionate VALID-Diet framework for artificial intelligence-generated dietary advice
papers.summary: Generative artificial intelligence can produce menus, recipes, shopping lists, and dietary explanations that appear individualized and clinically informed. Fluency alone, however, provides little evidence of nutritional accuracy, safety, feasibility, or benefit. We propose VALID-Diet, a staged framework for evaluating systems that generate actionable dietary recommendations as sociotechnical interventions. Its domains are Verification of nutritional targets and composition; Adversarial safety and boundary testing; Linkage between user inputs and recommendation changes; Implementation feasibility and inclusion; and Documentation, versioning, and reproducibility. Stage 0 defines intended use, input integrity, and a structured risk profile based on harm severity, exposure, autonomy, reversibility, and enforceable oversight. Stage 1 separates target validity, menu achievement, and arithmetic agreement and, for integrated systems, tests retrieval, calculation, and generation as distinct components. Stage 2 evaluates safety, substantive personalization, feasibility, and inclusion using pre-specified case blueprints. Stage 3 evaluates human oversight, workflow utility, and prospective outcomes only after earlier gates are passed. A retrospective worked application to a published retrieval-augmented personalized-nutrition system illustrates risk assignment and progression decisions. VA

papers.title: A scoping review of trust in firsthand and secondhand communication involving humans and artificial intelligence
papers.summary: Conversational and generative artificial intelligence (AI) systems increasingly create and pass information between people. This can make it hard to see who created a claim, whether it was changed, and whom to trust. Many studies examine firsthand human-human and human-AI communication, but less is known about secondhand communication, in which AI or another actor passes on a claim made elsewhere. In these cases, a human decision maker must evaluate the claim and the people or systems that created or passed it on. We present a scoping review built around six minimal motifs that represent firsthand or secondhand communication routes. Humans or AI systems may serve as the source or intermediary, while the decision maker remains human. We screened 3810 records and coded 124 studies to identify 21 trust factors in four dimensions: Decision Maker, Messenger, Message Property, and Environment. Qualitative synthesis also identified four recurring route-level patterns: distorted trust calibration, trust transfer, extremity amplification, and accountability diffusion. These patterns guide future research on AI-mediated communication. Overall, this review provides shared terms and a route-based framework for studying trust in multi-party human-AI communication and designing AI-mediated communication systems.

papers.title: The transformative power of artificial intelligence and machine learning in blood banking/transfusion medicine: A vein‐to‐vein approach from blood collection to transfusion services: On behalf of the AABB Foundation
papers.summary: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) are poised to transform transfusion medicine across the vein-to-vein continuum, from donor recruitment to recipient outcomes. Large datasets generated from millions of donations and transfusions create opportunities for predictive modeling, precision medicine, improved safety, and operational efficiency. This review outlines key applications of AI in blood banking and transfusion medicine using a comprehensive vein-to-vein framework. METHODS: The review synthesizes perspectives from blood services and hospital-based transfusion practices. Applications are discussed across donor recruitment, collections, testing, inventory management, hospital transfusion services, and education. Finally, AI safety, including ethical, regulatory, privacy, and implementation challenges, is addressed. This is a narrative, non-exhaustive review; given the rapidly evolving pace of AI/ML capabilities, this synthesis should be interpreted as a framework for ongoing surveillance rather than a fixed inventory of applications. RESULTS: Donor-focused applications include personalized recruitment, individualized iron management, and fairness auditing to reduce inequities. In supply chain operations, ML can improve demand forecasting, minimize waste, and optimize inventory. Federated learning may support multi-institutional collaboration without

papers.title: No One to Blame: A Framework of Constitutive AI Unaccountability
papers.summary: The increasing deployment of autonomous, agentic AI systems challenges traditional accountability mechanisms. Existing research predominantly frames AI accountability gaps as barriers that can be overcome through better standards, transparency, and institutional reform. We argue that this framing is insufficient: certain configurations of actors, systems, and institutions render AI accountability conceptually unachievable regardless of effort. We introduce the concept of constitutive AI unaccountability to capture these configurations. Through a three-stage qualitative study comprising a concept-centric literature analysis, a secondary analysis of 27 expert interviews with AI professionals from technical, legal, and sociotechnical backgrounds, and an illustrative framework application to the open-source agentic AI system OpenClaw, we identify nine categories and 20 themes of constitutive AI unaccountability. These are organized across structural, technological, and normative clusters and reinforce one another through eight directed interdependencies. Our framework is operationalized as a diagnostic instrument of 20 questions, which detected 17 of 20 conditions when applied to OpenClaw, including an inverted anthropomorphism configuration in which the AI agent was the only identifiable actor. We contribute a reframing of AI unaccountability as a constitutive property of sociotec

papers.title: Who Will Become the Next Senior? How Generative AI Erodes the Development Pathway in Software Engineering
papers.summary: Generative AI (GenAI) is reshaping software engineering, raising concerns about how the development pathway through which juniors become seniors is being eroded. While macro statistics show a decline in junior hiring and controlled studies demonstrate the effects of AI on individual task performance, the mechanisms through which GenAI reshapes early-career development in real organizational and educational contexts have not been thoroughly examined. Through 14 semi-structured interviews with juniors at the threshold of entering software engineering and senior software engineers in South Korea, analyzed using Reflexive Thematic Analysis, we reveal a foundational pattern of Absorption---GenAI redirects entry-level work into senior–AI workflows---and three consequences: (1) juniors losing the productive struggle through which expertise once developed; (2) the structural reproduction of this loss through collective normalization of GenAI use in university classrooms; and (3) the perceptual asymmetry between seniors and juniors that prevents either side from correcting these dynamics on their own. By extending learning theory and situated cognition to organizational and institutional scales, we argue that GenAI appears to be absorbing not just specific categories of tasks but also parts of the pathway through which the next generation of seniors is formed. papers.title: Epistemic Trustworthiness in Generative AI: A Normative Framework for Warranted Reliance in High-Stakes Workflows
papers.summary: Generative AI systems are increasingly deployed in high-stakes professional contexts, where their outputs shape what users believe, how they reason, and what they treat as settled. This raises a central question for responsible AI: under what conditions is reliance on generative AI outputs epistemically warranted rather than behaviourally induced? Existing frameworks largely ask whether AI outputs are accurate, fair, explainable, safe, or trusted by users. These questions remain necessary, and each can contribute to warranted reliance. However, they do not directly specify warranted reliance as a distinct evaluative target: the conditions under which users are justified in treating AI outputs as inputs into their own reasoning. We argue that this requires an account of epistemic trustworthiness: what makes a system epistemically worthy of reliance. Drawing on philosophical accounts of trustworthiness as competence and audience-orientation, we develop a constitutive normative framework comprising three jointly necessary and non-fungible conditions. First, epistemic humility requires systems to represent and communicate the limits of their competence. Second, epistemic access requires systems to enable users to inspect, question, and contest outputs in context. Third, resistance to epistemic injustice requires systems to recognise users as legitimate epistemic agents and avoid ma

papers.title: Frictionless Validation: Exploring AI Sycophancy and Developmental Risks
papers.summary: Adolescence is a critical period for the development of executive function, emotional regulation, and moral reasoning, all of which depend on cognitive and social resistance to mature properly. AI sycophancy, the tendency of language models to validate rather than challenge users, can reduce this resistance. In adults, sycophantic AI interactions have been shown to reduce prosocial intentions and inflate false conviction even after a single interaction. Whether analogous risks manifest differently across adolescent developmental stages remains unexamined. We address this using age-calibrated conversational probes across three developmental configurations spanning late childhood through adolescence: early (7–9), middle (10–12), and late (13–17), to evaluate four frontier consumer models on emotional, framing, and epistemic sycophancy dimensions not captured by existing benchmarks. Our central finding is exposure-side rather than a claim about realized developmental harm: raw emotional sycophancy peaks in late developmental probe conditions for three of four models, showing that models do not expose younger users to uniformly higher sycophancy. We document a 6.3× gap between models in emotional sycophancy and show that three models exceed an adult-effect calibration threshold under early developmental probe conditions. These output patterns align with theoretically distinct devel

papers.title: A Preliminary Generative Relational Ethics of Volunteer Intervention
papers.summary: This preliminary paper develops a Generative Relational ethics of volunteer intervention centered on situated agents, their candidate actions and omissions, affected subjects, historically acquired commitments, and the grounds required to justify practical conduct. It distinguishes the three GR reality levels and inherits relational descriptions and provenance tools from earlier papers without deriving moral duties from descriptive structures. A typed ethical-situation record supports evidence-relative assessments of need, testimony, competence, consent, urgent assistance, delegation, historically conditioned responsibility, restraint, and recipient participation. Candidate moral reasons and conditional deontic classifications remain distinct from verified organizational or legal authority and from Paper VI's institutional justice claims. The paper examines supererogation, volunteer well-being, dependence, distributed burdens, and the obligations that may arise when an accepted undertaking is revised or discontinued. Four wholly hypothetical diagnostic cases and a verification architecture test the completeness of subject and option coverage, evidential provenance, causal explanation, normative uncertainty, and practical robustness. The philosophical comparison maintains the independent grounds of deontological, consequentialist, care-ethical, virtue-ethical, and contractualist

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: AI-Driven Smart Irrigation System Using Edge-Based Embedded Controllers
papers.summary: This study brings out a new AI-based smart irrigation device aimed at solving the increasing problem of water shortage and poor agricultural procedures using emulated edge-based controllers. This combination of environmental sensing, lightweight machine learning algorithms and actuation on microcontrollers enables the system to do real time, adaptive irrigation scheduling. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. This was done by conducting extensive field tests within the semi-arid agricultural areas to prove the efficacy of the recommended solution. papers.title: STRATEGIC HUMAN RESOURCE MANAGEMENT, DIGITAL COMMERCE, AND AI-DRIVEN MARKETING: AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK FOR SUSTAINABLE BUSINESS GROWTH AND ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE
papers.summary: Digital transformation has intensified the need for organizations to align workforce strategy, digital commerce systems, and intelligent marketing capabilities. This comprehensive review examines how strategic human resource management, digital commerce, and AI-driven marketing support sustainable business growth and organizational performance. The review synthesizes literature on digital workforce planning, reskilling, platform-based commerce, marketing automation, predictive analytics, customer personalization, employee engagement, organizational resilience, and ethical governance. The findings indicate that strategic human resource management provides the capability foundation by developing digital skills, adaptive leadership, cross-functional collaboration, and continuous learning. Digital commerce serves as the value-creation and delivery infrastructure through online platforms, fintech integration, omnichannel systems, and network-based business models. AI-driven marketing serves as the customer-intelligence mechanism by enabling segmentation, forecasting, automation, personalization, and real-time engagement. Their coordinated integration can strengthen innovation, productivity, customer experience, revenue generation, and resilience. papers.title: Accurate and Robust Measurement of Single-Molecule Fluorescence Spectral Heterogeneity
papers.summary: Abstract Understanding single-molecule fluorescence spectral heterogeneity (smFLUSH) is vital for developing new probes for multidimensional super-resolution microscopy and decoding nanoscopic environments. However, traditional analysis methods distort the data and fail to distinguish random background noise for actual spectral differences between the single molecules. To overcome this bottleneck, we developed a Monte Carlo simulation and an adaptive signal processing framework inspired by balanced detection in spectral domain optical coherence tomography that employs a dynamically scaling, molecule-specific spectral boundary to effectively decouple intrinsic molecular fluctuations from instrumental noise, achieving an exceptional subnanometer precision floor. We experimentally validated this framework using a tailor-designed library of Boron Dipyrromethene (BODIPY) dyes engineered with systematically tuned degrees of conformational freedom. papers.title: When Words Change the Model: Sensitivity of LLMs for Constraint Programming Modelling
papers.summary: Abstract Automatically deriving executable and efficient constraint programming models from natural language descriptions has long been a central goal in optimisation and constraint programming. Large Language Models (LLMs) appear to bring this vision closer, showing promising results in generating models for classical benchmark problems. However, part of this apparent success may stem from data contamination rather than genuine reasoning capabilities, as many standard CP problems are likely represented in the training data of modern LLMs. In this initial investigation, we study the robustness of LLM-based constraint modelling by rephrasing and perturbing a set of 10 constraint problems while preserving their underlying structure. The modifications alter contextual elements and introduce misleading or distracting information to explore whether models rely on semantic understanding or superficial textual cues. We compare the models generated by three representative LLMs across the original and modified problem descriptions. Our qualitative analysis shows that, although LLMs frequently produce syntactically valid and semantically plausible models, their performance degrades significantly under contextual and linguistic variation, suggesting strong sensitivity to wording and contextual cues.

papers.title: Perception of AI-induced occupational replacement risk and withdrawal behavior: an identity threat perspective in the workplace
papers.summary: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly integrated into the workplace, the risk that occupations will be replaced by AI has received widespread attention. Nevertheless, the underlying mechanisms linking AI-induced occupational replacement risk perception to individual withdrawal behaviors remain underexplored. Taking identity threat as an explanatory lens, this study integrates Identity Threat Theory (ITT) and Technology Threat Avoidance Theory (TTAT) to investigate the effect of occupational replacement risk perception on employee withdrawal behavior, with professional identity, work meaningfulness, and job insecurity serving as mediators and technological self-efficacy as a moderator. Two studies were conducted to test the theoretical model developed in this research. Study 1 developed and validated the AI-induced occupational replacement risk perception scale. Study 2 employed a three-wave time-lagged survey design to test the hypotheses. The results show that occupational replacement risk perception is positively associated with withdrawal behavior through decreased professional identity and work meaningfulness as well as increased job insecurity. Furthermore, these indirect effects are weaker among employees with higher technological self-efficacy.
